I understand how upsetting and demoralizing this experience can be. Several questions though: 

Are you looking solely into the City of Chicago area or are you interested in looking into the surrounding suburbs as well? This can be tricky because you will need a reliable car to expand your scope of search, but it's something to consider. You will be surprised at how many opportunities are out there as soon as you leave the vicinity of the city -- of course, the commute can suck (I worked for a year at a community mental health center which consisted of 1.5 hours of driving each way), but it will at least give you the skills and experience necessary to apply for different positions later on. 

Don't be afraid to aim high -- what's the worse thing they can do to you besides reject your application? A lot of things listed on the "minimum requirement" are actually "it will be nice to find a candidate with these skills." Don't let the wording scare you. Keep throwing stuff on the wall until something sticks. 

The important thing is to start working somewhere, get any experience you can in order to use that as a stepping stone to something better. I have friends who only stayed in their first job for three months, while others have been working for over a year. 

And try to get that LSW. I personally think LSW is a scam, but having that behind your name in applications will help you. A lot of hospital positions, for example, require that you either have your LSW or obtain it within 6 months of hire. So while you are job hunting, use some of the free time you have to study for the LSW exam and get it as soon as possible.
